---- MODULE W4Od5m3p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Nodes, NoNode

ASSUME NoNode \notin Nodes

VARIABLES leader, up, pool, handoff, seated

vars == <<leader, up, pool, handoff, seated>>

\* handoff is an unordered bag of outstanding seating messages: Apply may take
\* any of them, so nothing about the emission order survives into delivery.
TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}
  /\ up \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ pool \subseteq Players
  /\ handoff \subseteq Players
  /\ seated \subseteq Players

\* The roster is conserved: every registered player occupies exactly one of the
\* three places, so the three sets always partition Players.
RosterConserved ==
  /\ pool \cup handoff \cup seated = Players
  /\ pool \cap handoff = {}
  /\ pool \cap seated = {}
  /\ handoff \cap seated = {}

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoNode
  /\ up = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
  /\ pool = Players
  /\ handoff = {}
  /\ seated = {}

Elect(n) ==
  /\ leader = NoNode
  /\ up[n]
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, pool, handoff, seated>>

\* Failover: losing the acting coordinator only vacates the seat; the roster
\* placement of every player is untouched by the failure.
Crash(n) ==
  /\ up[n]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NoNode ELSE leader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, handoff, seated>>

Restart(n) ==
  /\ ~up[n]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, pool, handoff, seated>>

Emit(p) ==
  /\ leader # NoNode
  /\ up[leader]
  /\ p \in pool
  /\ pool' = pool \ {p}
  /\ handoff' = handoff \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, seated>>

Apply(p) ==
  /\ p \in handoff
  /\ handoff' = handoff \ {p}
  /\ seated' = seated \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, pool>>

LeaveMatch(p) ==
  /\ p \in seated
  /\ seated' = seated \ {p}
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, up, handoff>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n) \/ Crash(n) \/ Restart(n)
  \/ \E p \in Players : Emit(p) \/ Apply(p) \/ LeaveMatch(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps a fixed roster of registered players. A small
group of matchmaker nodes runs the service, and exactly one of them at a time acts as the
elected coordinator; if the acting coordinator crashes the seat is vacated and a surviving
node can be elected in its place, so the service continues after failover. A crashed node
may later be restarted and becomes eligible for election again.

Every player sits in exactly one of three places: the open lobby pool, an in-flight seating
handoff, or a seated match. The coordinator moves a pooled player into the handoff stage by
emitting a seating message naming that player. Seating messages travel over an unordered
channel: the handoff stage is a bag of outstanding messages with no delivery order at all,
so messages issued earlier may be applied later and vice versa. When a seating message is
applied, the named player leaves the handoff stage and takes a seat in a match. A seated
player may leave the match at any time and returns directly to the open lobby pool.

Nothing in the system may invent a player or lose one: the roster is a conserved quantity
that only ever moves between the three places, never grows and never shrinks. The actions
are: elect a coordinator, crash a node (vacating the coordinator seat if it held it),
restart a crashed node, emit a seating message for a pooled player, apply an outstanding
seating message in any order, and leave a match back to the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lobby pool, the outstanding-handoff set, and the seated set are always
pairwise disjoint and together contain exactly the full registered roster, so no player is
ever duplicated across two places or lost from all three.

---- MODULE W4Od2m5p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Packs, Quorum, MaxOverride

ASSUME Quorum \in 1..Cardinality(Robots)

VARIABLES proposed, votes, retired, permit, forced, budget

vars == <<proposed, votes, retired, permit, forced, budget>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ proposed \subseteq Packs
  /\ votes \in [Packs -> SUBSET Robots]
  /\ retired \subseteq Packs
  /\ permit \in [Packs -> 0..1]
  /\ forced \subseteq Packs
  /\ budget \in 0..MaxOverride

\* A standing proposal is mandated by a quorum of robot votes, or by one
\* privileged admin stamp. A mandate is never taken back.
Mandated(p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ (Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum \/ p \in forced)

Init ==
  /\ proposed = {}
  /\ votes = [p \in Packs |-> {}]
  /\ retired = {}
  /\ permit = [p \in Packs |-> 1]
  /\ forced = {}
  /\ budget = MaxOverride

\* The permit is the one-shot capability: crushing spends it, and a pack with a
\* spent permit is exactly a pack already on the retirement record.
OneShotCrush == \A p \in Packs : (permit[p] = 0) <=> (p \in retired)

Propose(p) ==
  /\ p \notin proposed
  /\ permit[p] = 1
  /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, retired, permit, forced, budget>>

CastVote(r, p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ r \notin votes[p]
  /\ permit[p] = 1
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {r}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, retired, permit, forced, budget>>

AdminStamp(p) ==
  /\ budget > 0
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ p \notin forced
  /\ permit[p] = 1
  /\ forced' = forced \cup {p}
  /\ budget' = budget - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, retired, permit>>

Withdraw(p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ ~Mandated(p)
  /\ proposed' = proposed \ {p}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<retired, permit, forced, budget>>

Crush(p) ==
  /\ Mandated(p)
  /\ permit[p] = 1
  /\ retired' = retired \cup {p}
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, forced, budget>>

CrushStep == \E p \in Packs : Crush(p)

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Packs : Propose(p) \/ AdminStamp(p) \/ Withdraw(p)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, p \in Packs : CastVote(r, p)
  \/ CrushStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(CrushStep)

EventualCrush == \A p \in Packs : Mandated(p) ~> (p \in retired)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2}
  Packs = {k1, k2, k3}
  Quorum = 2
  MaxOverride = 1

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT OneShotCrush
PROPERTY EventualCrush
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet retires worn battery packs. Retiring a pack is irreversible: the
pack is physically crushed, so each pack carries exactly one single-use disposal permit
that the crusher consumes when it runs, and a pack whose permit is already spent can never
be presented again.

A pack is first put forward for retirement by any robot. Robots then cast individual votes
on the standing proposal; a proposal carries a mandate once a quorum of distinct robots has
voted for it. A yard supervisor holds a privileged admin override and may stamp a standing
proposal as mandated without any votes at all, but the override budget is finite and each
stamp spends one unit of it. A proposal that has not yet gained a mandate may be withdrawn,
which clears its collected votes; once a proposal is mandated it can no longer be withdrawn
and the mandate stands. The crusher runs against any mandated pack that still holds its
permit: the run records the retirement and spends the permit in the same step.

The actions are: propose a pack for retirement, cast a robot vote on a standing proposal,
spend one admin override to stamp a standing proposal as mandated, withdraw a proposal that
has no mandate yet, and run the crusher on a mandated pack.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A pack's single-use disposal permit is spent if and only if that pack is on
the retirement record, so no pack can ever be crushed a second time and no retirement can be
recorded without consuming the pack's one permit.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every pack whose proposal gains a mandate, whether by quorum or by admin
override, is eventually crushed and appears on the retirement record.

---- MODULE W4Od7m5p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Boxes, Quorum, MaxBays

ASSUME Quorum \in 1..Cardinality(Cranes)

VARIABLES ballot, tally, inHold, capacity, hatch

vars == <<ballot, tally, inHold, capacity, hatch>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ ballot \in [Boxes -> {"quay", "open", "sealed"}]
  /\ tally \in [Boxes -> SUBSET Cranes]
  /\ inHold \subseteq Boxes
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxBays
  /\ hatch \in BOOLEAN

Occupancy == Cardinality(inHold)

\* A lowering is irreversible, so the ballot that authorised it is spent on the
\* way down: sealed, with the crane tally wiped.
SpentBallot == \A b \in Boxes : b \in inHold => (ballot[b] = "sealed" /\ tally[b] = {})

Init ==
  /\ ballot = [b \in Boxes |-> "quay"]
  /\ tally = [b \in Boxes |-> {}]
  /\ inHold = {}
  /\ capacity = 1
  /\ hatch = FALSE

OpenBallot(b) ==
  /\ ballot[b] = "quay"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![b] = "open"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, inHold, capacity, hatch>>

CastVote(c, b) ==
  /\ ballot[b] = "open"
  /\ c \notin tally[b]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, inHold, capacity, hatch>>

\* Lowering needs a quorum, an open hatch and a free bay; capacity is read at
\* the moment of the lift, not reserved in advance.
Lower(b) ==
  /\ ballot[b] = "open"
  /\ Cardinality(tally[b]) >= Quorum
  /\ hatch
  /\ Occupancy < capacity
  /\ inHold' = inHold \cup {b}
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![b] = "sealed"]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, hatch>>

RigMoreBays ==
  /\ ~hatch
  /\ capacity < MaxBays
  /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, tally, inHold, hatch>>

StripBays ==
  /\ ~hatch
  /\ capacity > 1
  /\ capacity - 1 >= Occupancy
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, tally, inHold, hatch>>

WorkHatch ==
  /\ hatch' = ~hatch
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, tally, inHold, capacity>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Boxes : OpenBallot(b) \/ Lower(b)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, b \in Boxes : CastVote(c, b)
  \/ RigMoreBays \/ StripBays \/ WorkHatch

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {c1, c2}
  Boxes = {b1, b2, b3}
  Quorum = 2
  MaxBays = 3

INVARIANT SpentBallot
nl:
A container-ship crane yard lowers containers into a ship's hold. Lowering a container is
irreversible for the voyage: once a box is down in the hold and lashed, the yard cranes
cannot lift it back out, so the yard must never be able to run the lowering procedure for
the same container twice.

Each container gets a ballot. The gang of yard cranes opens a ballot for a container that
is still on the quay, and individual cranes then vote on that ballot. A container may be
lowered only when a quorum of distinct cranes has voted for it, the hold hatch is open, and
the hold still has free space. Lowering seals the container's ballot and clears its tally,
so the ballot is spent and no fresh mandate can ever be assembled for that box again.

The hold's free space is not fixed. The deck crew re-rigs lashing bays while the hatch is
closed, raising or lowering the hold's working capacity during the operation; capacity is
never dropped below the number of boxes already down. The hatch itself is opened and closed
by the deck crew between lifts.

The actions are: open a ballot for a quay container, cast a crane vote on an open ballot,
lower a mandated container into the hold (sealing its ballot and clearing its tally), raise
the hold capacity, reduce the hold capacity down to but not below current occupancy, and
open or close the hatch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every container already down in the hold has a sealed ballot with an empty
tally, so no container in the hold can ever accumulate a fresh quorum and be lowered a
second time.

---- MODULE W4Od2m3p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Docks, Controllers

NoDock == "nodock"
NoRobot == "norobot"
Vacant == "vacant"

VARIABLES phase, owner, assigned, inService, dispatcher, up

vars == <<phase, owner, assigned, inService, dispatcher, up>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Robots -> {"idle", "waiting", "docked", "charged"}]
  /\ owner \in [Docks -> Robots \cup {NoRobot}]
  /\ assigned \in [Robots -> Docks \cup {NoDock}]
  /\ inService \subseteq Docks
  /\ dispatcher \in Controllers \cup {Vacant}
  /\ up \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]

\* The two allocation records must be exact inverses; a dock handed to two
\* robots shows up immediately as a robot naming a dock that names someone else.
Mirrored == \A r \in Robots, d \in Docks : (assigned[r] = d) <=> (owner[d] = r)

Init ==
  /\ phase = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
  /\ owner = [d \in Docks |-> NoRobot]
  /\ assigned = [r \in Robots |-> NoDock]
  /\ inService = Docks
  /\ dispatcher = Vacant
  /\ up = [c \in Controllers |-> TRUE]

Elect(c) ==
  /\ dispatcher = Vacant /\ up[c]
  /\ dispatcher' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, owner, assigned, inService, up>>

Crash(c) ==
  /\ up[c]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ dispatcher' = IF dispatcher = c THEN Vacant ELSE dispatcher
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, owner, assigned, inService>>

Restart(c) ==
  /\ ~up[c]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, owner, assigned, inService, dispatcher>>

AskCharge(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "idle"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, assigned, inService, dispatcher, up>>

\* Only a live dispatcher allocates, and only a free, in-service dock.
Send(r, d) ==
  /\ dispatcher # Vacant /\ up[dispatcher]
  /\ phase[r] = "waiting"
  /\ d \in inService /\ owner[d] = NoRobot
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![d] = r]
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = d]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "docked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, dispatcher, up>>

Finish(r) ==
  /\ phase[r] = "docked"
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![assigned[r]] = NoRobot]
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = NoDock]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "charged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, dispatcher, up>>

\* Runtime capacity change: maintenance never strands the last dock.
PullDock(d) ==
  /\ d \in inService /\ owner[d] = NoRobot /\ Cardinality(inService) > 1
  /\ inService' = inService \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, owner, assigned, dispatcher, up>>

ReturnDock(d) ==
  /\ d \notin inService
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, owner, assigned, dispatcher, up>>

ElectStep == \E c \in Controllers : Elect(c)
RestartStep == \E c \in Controllers : Restart(c)
SendStep == \E r \in Robots, d \in Docks : Send(r, d)
FinishStep == \E r \in Robots : Finish(r)

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Elect(c) \/ Crash(c) \/ Restart(c)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : AskCharge(r) \/ Finish(r)
  \/ \E d \in Docks : PullDock(d) \/ ReturnDock(d)
  \/ SendStep

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(RestartStep) /\ SF_vars(ElectStep)
  /\ SF_vars(SendStep) /\ SF_vars(FinishStep)

Docking ==
  \A r \in Robots : (phase[r] = "waiting") ~> (phase[r] \in {"docked", "charged"})
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a bank of charging docks. A small set of fleet controllers
runs the assignment service; at most one controller at a time holds the dispatcher role,
and only the current dispatcher may hand a dock to a robot. A controller can crash, which
vacates the dispatcher role if that controller held it, and a crashed controller can be
brought back up and stand for the role again.

The assignment is recorded twice, as it is in the real system: the dock bank records which
robot occupies each dock, and each robot records which dock it was sent to. These two
records must stay exact inverses of one another, because that is what stops the dispatcher
from handing one dock to two different robots.

A robot starts idle, asks for a charge, is sent to a dock by the dispatcher, and once it has
finished charging it releases the dock and is done. The number of docks actually in service
changes during operation: maintenance can pull an empty dock out of service and put it back
later, but never the last remaining in-service dock, so at least one dock is always usable.
The dispatcher only ever sends a robot to a free, in-service dock.

The actions are: elect a dispatcher from the live controllers, crash a controller (vacating
the role if it was the dispatcher), restart a crashed controller, a robot asks for a charge,
the dispatcher sends a waiting robot to a free in-service dock, a charging robot finishes
and releases its dock, pull an empty dock out of service, and return a dock to service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The dock bank's occupancy record and the robots' own dock records are
always exact inverses -- a robot names a dock if and only if that dock names that robot --
so no dock is ever allocated to two robots at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every robot that asks for a charge is eventually sent to a dock.

---- MODULE W4Od15m1p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumFirms, Symbols

Firms == 1..NumFirms

\* The baton walks the ring; only its holder may run an uncross.
Succ(f) == (f % NumFirms) + 1

VARIABLES baton, tape, seen, slow, book

vars == <<baton, tape, seen, slow, book>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Firms
  /\ tape \subseteq Symbols
  /\ seen \in [Firms -> SUBSET Symbols]
  /\ slow \in [Firms -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ book \subseteq Symbols

\* A firm's local print record only ever trails the authoritative tape; it may
\* be behind, never ahead, so no lagging firm can invent a second print.
ViewsTrailTape == \A f \in Firms : seen[f] \subseteq tape

Init ==
  /\ baton = 1
  /\ tape = {}
  /\ seen = [f \in Firms |-> {}]
  /\ slow = [f \in Firms |-> FALSE]
  /\ book = {}

Admit(s) ==
  /\ s \notin book
  /\ book' = book \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, tape, seen, slow>>

PassBaton ==
  /\ baton' = Succ(baton)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tape, seen, slow, book>>

\* Authorisation reads the tape, not the holder's own record.
Uncross(s) ==
  /\ s \in book
  /\ s \notin tape
  /\ ~slow[baton]
  /\ tape' = tape \cup {s}
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![baton] = @ \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, slow, book>>

Refresh(f, s) ==
  /\ s \in tape
  /\ s \notin seen[f]
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![f] = @ \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, tape, slow, book>>

FallBehind(f) ==
  /\ ~slow[f]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, tape, seen, book>>

CatchUp(f) ==
  /\ slow[f]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, tape, seen, book>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E s \in Symbols : Admit(s) \/ Uncross(s)
  \/ \E f \in Firms : FallBehind(f) \/ CatchUp(f)
  \/ \E f \in Firms, s \in Symbols : Refresh(f, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  NumFirms = 3
  Symbols = {aa, bb}

INVARIANT ViewsTrailTape
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction. Member firms sit in a fixed ring and a single
baton travels around it; only the firm currently holding the baton may run an uncross and
publish the opening print for a symbol. Publishing an opening print is irreversible -- the
print goes out on the public tape and can never be withdrawn or reissued -- so the exchange
must run the uncross for a given symbol at most once.

A symbol first has to be admitted into the auction book. The firm holding the baton may then
uncross an admitted symbol whose print is not yet on the tape; doing so writes the print to
the exchange's single authoritative tape and, in the same step, into that firm's own local
record. The baton is passed on around the ring at any time.

Firms can be slow, but they never fail. A slow firm is still grinding through its imbalance
calculation and will not run an uncross while it is behind; the baton simply moves past it.
Every firm keeps a local record of the prints it knows about, and a lagging firm refreshes
that record from the tape one symbol at a time, so a firm's local record trails the tape.
An uncross is authorised against the authoritative tape, never against the firm's own
possibly-lagging record, which is what stops a slow firm from printing a symbol twice.

The actions are: admit a symbol into the auction book, pass the baton to the next firm in
the ring, uncross an admitted symbol that is not yet on the tape, refresh one lagging firm's
local record from the tape, mark a firm slow, and mark a slow firm caught up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every firm's local print record is always a subset of the exchange's single
authoritative tape, so no firm ever holds a print the exchange did not make and no symbol's
opening print can be issued a second time from a lagging local view.

---- MODULE W4Od12m3p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Servers, Units, MaxTerm

NoServer == "noserver"

\* The registry pointer may name a stopped server, or nobody at all.
CoordDown(c, a) == IF c \in Servers THEN ~a[c] ELSE TRUE

VARIABLES alive, myTerm, regTerm, coord, ledger

vars == <<alive, myTerm, regTerm, coord, ledger>>

Dispatched == { ledger[i].unit : i \in 1..Len(ledger) }

TypeOK ==
  /\ alive \in [Servers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ myTerm \in [Servers -> 0..MaxTerm]
  /\ regTerm \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ coord \in Servers \cup {NoServer}
  /\ ledger \in Seq([unit: Units, term: 0..MaxTerm])

\* Each record is stamped with the writer's OWN remembered term, so a recovered
\* stale server writing to the ledger would push the stamps backwards.
LedgerTermsMonotone ==
  \A i \in 1..Len(ledger) : \A j \in 1..i : ledger[j].term <= ledger[i].term

Init ==
  /\ alive = [s \in Servers |-> TRUE]
  /\ myTerm = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
  /\ regTerm = 0
  /\ coord = NoServer
  /\ ledger = <<>>

\* A silent stop: the registry's coordinator pointer is deliberately not cleared.
CrashSilently(s) ==
  /\ alive[s]
  /\ regTerm < MaxTerm
  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<myTerm, regTerm, coord, ledger>>

Recover(s) ==
  /\ ~alive[s]
  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<myTerm, regTerm, coord, ledger>>

Handover(s) ==
  /\ regTerm < MaxTerm
  /\ CoordDown(coord, alive)
  /\ alive[s]
  /\ regTerm' = regTerm + 1
  /\ myTerm' = [myTerm EXCEPT ![s] = regTerm + 1]
  /\ coord' = s
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, ledger>>

Dispatch(s, u) ==
  /\ alive[s]
  /\ coord = s
  /\ myTerm[s] = regTerm
  /\ u \notin Dispatched
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, [unit |-> u, term |-> myTerm[s]])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, myTerm, regTerm, coord>>

RecoverStep == \E s \in Servers : Recover(s)
HandoverStep == \E s \in Servers : Handover(s)
DispatchStep == \E s \in Servers, u \in Units : Dispatch(s, u)

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Servers : CrashSilently(s) \/ Recover(s) \/ Handover(s)
  \/ DispatchStep

\* Recovery and handover are strongly fair, so a dead coordinator is always
\* replaced and the ledger keeps filling.
Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(RecoverStep) /\ SF_vars(HandoverStep) /\ SF_vars(DispatchStep)

EventualDispatch == \A u \in Units : <>(u \in Dispatched)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Servers = {s1, s2}
  Units = {u1, u2}
  MaxTerm = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT LedgerTermsMonotone
PROPERTY EventualDispatch
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker runs on a couple of branch servers. One server at a time is
recognised as the coordinator, and the recognition carries a term number: the registry holds
the current term, and each server remembers the term under which it last believed itself to
be coordinator.

A server can crash silently -- it simply stops, without notifying anyone and without the
registry clearing its coordinator pointer. A crashed server may come back up later still
remembering its old term, which is exactly the dangerous case: it thinks it is coordinator
but the world has moved on. When the registry observes that the recognised coordinator is
down (or that there is none yet), it bumps the term and recognises some live server under
the new term. The registry only tolerates a bounded number of such handovers, and no server
crashes once that bound is reached.

Dispatching a unit of blood to a hospital appends a record to the branch's shared dispatch
ledger, and the record is stamped with the term the dispatching server itself believes it
holds -- not with the registry's term. A dispatch is only accepted from the live, recognised
coordinator whose remembered term matches the registry's current term. That check is what
keeps a recovered, stale server from writing to the ledger. Each unit is dispatched at most
once.

The actions are: a server crashes silently, a crashed server comes back up still holding its

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {ca, cb}
  Airlines = {al1, al2}
  TotalSlots = 3
  MaxRunways = 2
  Quorum = 2

INVARIANT SlotsConserved
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands out the arrival slots for one hour. The number of
arrival slots for that hour is fixed when the hour opens and cannot change: every slot is at
all times either sitting unallocated in the pool, held by one airline as a granted arrival,
or already spent by an aircraft that has landed. Slots are never minted and never vanish.

Granting a slot is a team decision. Controllers on duty each cast a vote for a pending grant
to a particular airline, and the grant only goes through once a quorum of distinct
controllers has voted for it; the tally is cleared as the grant is issued, so a fresh quorum
is needed for the next one. An airline that has been granted a slot may hand it back
unflown, in which case the slot returns to the unallocated pool, or may fly it, in which
case the slot is spent and the arrival is complete.

Runway capacity changes during the hour: runways open and close for weather and snow
clearing, and the number of slots that may be held outstanding at any moment is limited by
how many runways are currently open. A runway may only be closed if the outstanding grants
still fit on the runways that remain open.

The actions are: a controller votes for a pending grant to an airline, issue a granted slot
to an airline once its quorum is met and an open runway is available, an airline hands a
granted slot back to the pool, an airline flies its granted slot and spends it, open another
runway, and close a runway that is not needed by the outstanding grants.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The unallocated pool, the slots held by all airlines, and the slots already
spent by landings always add up to exactly the hour's fixed slot count.

NoBox == 0
Vacant == "vacant"

\* Box n weighs n tonnes, so the conservation sum is not a plain headcount.
Tons(b) == b

vars == <<quay, spreader, hold, leader, up>>

RECURSIVE Weigh(_)
Weigh(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
            ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN Tons(b) + Weigh(S \ {b})

RECURSIVE Hanging(_)
Hanging(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET c == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN (IF spreader[c] = NoBox THEN 0 ELSE Tons(spreader[c])) + Hanging(S \ {c})

  /\ quay \subseteq Boxes
  /\ spreader \in [Cranes -> Boxes \cup {NoBox}]
  /\ hold \subseteq Boxes
  /\ leader \in Cranes \cup {Vacant}
  /\ up \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]

\* Hanging tonnage is summed crane by crane, so a box hanging twice would be
\* counted twice and break the balance.
TonnageConserved == Weigh(quay) + Hanging(Cranes) + Weigh(hold) = Weigh(Boxes)

  /\ spreader = [c \in Cranes |-> NoBox]
  /\ hold = {}
  /\ leader = Vacant
  /\ up = [c \in Cranes |-> TRUE]

Elect(c) ==
  /\ leader = Vacant /\ up[c]
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quay, spreader, hold, up>>

\* Silent: the leader pointer is untouched by the failure itself.
CrashSilently(c) ==
  /\ up[c]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quay, spreader, hold, leader>>

NoticeDead ==
  /\ leader # Vacant /\ ~up[leader]
  /\ leader' = Vacant
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quay, spreader, hold, up>>

Pick(b) ==

  /\ spreader[leader] = NoBox
  /\ b \in quay
  /\ quay' = quay \ {b}
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![leader] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, leader, up>>

Lower(c) ==
  /\ up[c] /\ spreader[c] # NoBox
  /\ hold' = hold \cup {spreader[c]}
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = NoBox]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quay, leader, up>>

RecoverLoad(c) ==

  /\ hold' = hold \cup {spreader[c]}
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![c] = NoBox]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quay, leader, up>>

Restart(c) ==
  /\ ~up[c] /\ spreader[c] = NoBox
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<quay, spreader, hold, leader>>

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  NumBoxes = 3
  Cranes = {cr1, cr2}

INVARIANT TonnageConserved
PROPERTY Stowed
nl:
A container-ship crane yard loads a numbered set of boxes from the quay into a ship's hold.
Each box has a known tonnage, and the total tonnage on site is a conserved quantity: every
tonne is at any moment either standing on the quay, hanging from exactly one crane's
spreader, or already down in the hold. Steel is never created and never lost.

One crane at a time is the gang leader and is the only crane allowed to pick a box off the
quay. A crane can crash silently: its drive simply dies, with no signal to anyone, and the
gang's leader pointer keeps naming a crane that is no longer working. The gang notices this
separately and vacates the leader slot, after which a live crane can be elected leader. A
crashed crane that is hanging a box does not drop it -- the standby rigging gear lowers that
box the rest of the way into the hold -- and a crashed crane with an empty spreader can be
brought back up and stand for election again.

A loaded crane that is still alive lowers its box into the hold itself. Boxes only ever move
quay to spreader to hold; nothing ever travels back to the quay.

The actions are: elect a live crane as gang leader, crash a crane silently, the gang notices
the leader is dead and vacates the leader slot, the leader picks a box off the quay onto its
spreader, a live loaded crane lowers its box into the hold, the standby gear recovers a
crashed crane's hanging box into the hold, and a crashed empty crane comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tonnage on the quay, plus the tonnage hanging from the cranes counted
one crane at a time, plus the tonnage in the hold, always equals the site's total tonnage.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every box eventually ends up in the ship's hold.

CONSTANTS Blocks, Cabins

MaxVer == Cardinality(Blocks)

VARIABLES record, version, snapVer, snapVal, acked, up

vars == <<record, version, snapVer, snapVal, acked, up>>

NoSnap == -1

TypeOK ==
  /\ record \subseteq Blocks
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ snapVer \in [Cabins -> {NoSnap} \cup (0..MaxVer)]
  /\ snapVal \in [Cabins -> SUBSET Blocks]
  /\ acked \in [Cabins -> SUBSET Blocks]
  /\ up \in [Cabins -> BOOLEAN]

\* An acknowledged claim must still be readable in the shared record: a
\* stale-snapshot write-back would silently erase someone else's claim.
NoLostUpdate == \A c \in Cabins : acked[c] \subseteq record

Init ==
  /\ record = {}
  /\ version = 0
  /\ snapVer = [c \in Cabins |-> NoSnap]
  /\ snapVal = [c \in Cabins |-> {}]
  /\ acked = [c \in Cabins |-> {}]
  /\ up = [c \in Cabins |-> TRUE]

ReadRegister(c) ==
  /\ up[c]
  /\ snapVer[c] = NoSnap
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![c] = version]
  /\ snapVal' = [snapVal EXCEPT ![c] = record]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, acked, up>>

\* The swap only lands while the version still matches the read.
Swap(c, b) ==
  /\ up[c]
  /\ snapVer[c] = version
  /\ b \notin snapVal[c]
  /\ record' = snapVal[c] \cup {b}
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {b}]
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVal, up>>

Rejected(c) ==
  /\ up[c]
  /\ snapVer[c] # NoSnap
  /\ snapVer[c] # version
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
  /\ snapVal' = [snapVal EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, acked, up>>

\* Silent stop: the cabin keeps its snapshot across the outage.
CrashSilently(c) ==
  /\ up[c]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, snapVer, snapVal, acked>>

ComeBack(c) ==
  /\ ~up[c]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, snapVer, snapVal, acked>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cabins : ReadRegister(c) \/ Rejected(c) \/ CrashSilently(c) \/ ComeBack(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cabins, b \in Blocks : Swap(c, b)

nl:
A subway signalling system keeps one shared occupancy record for the line: the set of track
blocks that have been claimed during the shift. Several interlocking cabins update that
record, and they do it through a compare-and-swap register: the record is stored together
with a version counter.

A cabin works in two steps. First it reads the register, taking a private snapshot of both
the version and the record contents. Later it writes back the snapshot with one extra block
added, but the write only lands if the register's version is still the version the cabin
read; on success the register takes the new contents, the version advances by one, and the
cabin is given an acknowledgement for that block. If the version has moved on since the read
-- because another cabin got there first -- the write is rejected and the cabin drops its
snapshot and starts over. A cabin only ever claims a block that is not already in the record
it can see, so the record only ever grows.

A cabin can crash silently: it stops with no announcement, and it keeps whatever snapshot it
was holding, so when it is brought back up it may still be carrying a snapshot from before
its outage. A crashed cabin cannot write. The version check is exactly what makes that
recovered, out-of-date snapshot harmless.

The actions are: a live cabin reads the register into its snapshot, a live cabin's
compare-and-swap succeeds and its block is acknowledged, a cabin whose snapshot version is
out of date has its write rejected and discards the snapshot, a cabin crashes silently while
keeping its snapshot, and a crashed cabin comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every block a cabin has been acknowledged for is still present in the
shared occupancy record, so no acknowledged update is ever overwritten and lost.

Free == "free"

VARIABLES holder, book, confirmed, epoch, viewEpoch

vars == <<holder, book, confirmed, epoch, viewEpoch>>

  /\ holder \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {Free}]
  /\ book \in [Instances -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ confirmed \subseteq Slots
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ viewEpoch \in [Instances -> 0..MaxEpoch]

\* The two independent instances read one shared seat map; their private books
\* may lag behind reality only by being empty, never by claiming someone else's
\* slot. That is what rules out a slot held twice.
BooksAgree == \A i \in Instances : \A s \in Slots : s \in book[i] => holder[s] = i

Init ==
  /\ holder = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
  /\ book = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
  /\ confirmed = {}
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ viewEpoch = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, book, confirmed, viewEpoch>>

Loose(i) == book[i] \ confirmed

\* An epoch bump voids unconfirmed reservations; they go back to the pool.
GiveBack(i) ==

  /\ Loose(i) # {}
  /\ holder' = [s \in Slots |-> IF s \in Loose(i) THEN Free ELSE holder[s]]
  /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cap confirmed]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<confirmed, epoch, viewEpoch>>

  /\ Loose(i) = {}
  /\ viewEpoch' = [viewEpoch EXCEPT ![i] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, book, confirmed, epoch>>

Take(i, s) ==

  /\ holder[s] = Free
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = i]
  /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<confirmed, epoch, viewEpoch>>

  /\ s \in book[i]
  /\ s \notin confirmed
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, book, epoch, viewEpoch>>

AdoptStep == \E i \in Instances : AdoptEpoch(i)
TakeStep == \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : Take(i, s)
ConfirmStep == \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : Confirm(i, s)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Slots = {sa, sb}
  Instances = {portal, desk}
  MaxEpoch = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT BooksAgree
PROPERTY AllSeatsSettled
nl:
A university course-registration system runs two independent registration instances -- the
main portal and the advisers' desk -- against one shared pool of seats in a course. Each
seat is a slot that may be given to at most one instance's applicant. The shared seat map
records, for each slot, which instance currently holds it, and each instance also keeps its
own book of the slots it believes it holds. Those two records must never disagree.

The pool is reconfigured from time to time by the registrar, which bumps an epoch number.
The registrar only reconfigures a bounded number of times during a registration window. An
epoch bump voids every reservation that has not yet been confirmed: an instance whose view
epoch is behind must first give back all of its unconfirmed slots, returning them to the
pool, and only then may it pick up the new epoch. An instance may take a free slot or
confirm one of its own slots only while its view epoch matches the registrar's current
epoch. Confirmed slots are registrations of record and survive reconfiguration.

The actions are: the registrar reconfigures and bumps the epoch, an instance with a stale
view gives back its unconfirmed slots, an instance with a stale view and no unconfirmed
slots adopts the current epoch, an instance holding the current epoch takes a free slot from
the shared map into its own book, and an instance holding the current epoch confirms a slot
it holds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: If an instance's own book lists a slot, the shared seat map names that same
instance as the slot's holder, so a slot is never allocated to both instances at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every slot in the pool is eventually confirmed to an instance.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Batches, Slots, Banks

NoSlot == "noslot"
NoBatch == "nobatch"

VARIABLES phase, slot, votes, register, up

vars == <<phase, slot, votes, register, up>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Batches -> {"idle", "prepare", "committed", "aborted"}]
  /\ slot \in [Batches -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ votes \in [Batches -> SUBSET Banks]
  /\ register \in [Slots -> Batches \cup {NoBatch}]
  /\ up \in [Banks -> BOOLEAN]

\* The reservation is written in two books; a settled batch must still be the
\* one the slot register names, which is what forbids two batches per slot.
SlotHeldOnce ==
  \A b \in Batches :
    phase[b] = "committed" => (slot[b] \in Slots /\ register[slot[b]] = b)

Init ==
  /\ phase = [b \in Batches |-> "idle"]
  /\ slot = [b \in Batches |-> NoSlot]
  /\ votes = [b \in Batches |-> {}]
  /\ register = [s \in Slots |-> NoBatch]
  /\ up = [k \in Banks |-> TRUE]

Reserve(b, s) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "idle"
  /\ register[s] = NoBatch
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![b] = s]
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![s] = b]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "prepare"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, up>>

CastVote(k, b) ==
  /\ up[k]
  /\ phase[b] = "prepare"
  /\ k \notin votes[b]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {k}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, slot, register, up>>

CommitBatch(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "prepare"
  /\ votes[b] = Banks
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slot, votes, register, up>>

\* Timeout: the coordinator cannot see a silent crash, only a missing vote.
AbortBatch(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "prepare"
  /\ votes[b] # Banks
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "aborted"]
  /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![slot[b]] = NoBatch]
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![b] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, up>>

CrashSilently(k) ==
  /\ up[k]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![k] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, slot, votes, register>>

ComeBack(k) ==
  /\ ~up[k]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![k] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, slot, votes, register>>

  \/ \E b \in Batches, s \in Slots : Reserve(b, s)
  \/ \E k \in Banks, b \in Batches : CastVote(k, b)
  \/ \E b \in Batches : CommitBatch(b) \/ AbortBatch(b)
  \/ \E k \in Banks : CrashSilently(k) \/ ComeBack(k)

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement runs in batches. The clearing cycle has a small number of
settlement slots, and each batch that settles must occupy its own slot: two batches may
never settle into the same slot.

The coordinator drives each batch through a two-phase commit with the member banks. It first
reserves a free slot for the batch and writes the reservation into two places -- the batch
records which slot it took, and the slot register records which batch took it -- then moves
the batch into the prepare phase. Each member bank then votes for the batch. When every
member bank has voted, the coordinator commits the batch into its slot. If the coordinator
times out while any bank's vote is still missing, it aborts the batch and hands the slot
back, clearing both the batch's slot field and the slot register entry.

A member bank can crash silently: it stops voting with no announcement of any kind, so the
coordinator learns nothing and simply times out. A crashed bank may come back up later and
resume voting on batches still in the prepare phase.

The actions are: reserve a free slot for an idle batch and start its prepare phase, a live
bank votes for a batch in prepare, commit a batch whose votes are all in, abort a batch that
is still missing a vote and release its slot, a bank crashes silently, and a crashed bank
comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every committed batch, the slot register still names that batch as the
holder of the slot the batch settled into, so no slot is ever allocated to two batches.

VARIABLES feed, manifest, delivered, countdown

  /\ manifest \in [Halls -> SUBSET Bags]
  /\ delivered \subseteq Bags
  /\ countdown \in [Bags -> 0..LeaseLen]

\* Custody is exclusive and total: the feed, the two halls' manifests and the
\* delivered set partition the bags, so nothing is duplicated or dropped.
CustodyAccounted ==
  /\ feed \cup Held \cup delivered = Bags
  /\ feed \cap Held = {}
  /\ feed \cap delivered = {}
  /\ Held \cap delivered = {}
  /\ \A g, h \in Halls : g # h => manifest[g] \cap manifest[h] = {}

Init ==
  /\ feed = Bags
  /\ manifest = [h \in Halls |-> {}]
  /\ delivered = {}
  /\ countdown = [b \in Bags |-> 0]

TakeCustody(h, b) ==
  /\ b \in feed
  /\ Cardinality(manifest[h]) < MaxLoad
  /\ feed' = feed \ {b}
  /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![h] = @ \cup {b}]
  /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![b] = LeaseLen]
  /\ UNCHANGED delivered

Tick ==
  /\ \E b \in Held : countdown[b] > 0
  /\ countdown' = [b \in Bags |-> IF countdown[b] > 0 THEN countdown[b] - 1 ELSE 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feed, manifest, delivered>>

\* A void lease never strands its bag: custody returns to the shared feed.
LeaseVoid(h, b) ==
  /\ b \in manifest[h]
  /\ countdown[b] = 0
  /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![h] = @ \ {b}]
  /\ feed' = feed \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<delivered, countdown>>

Deliver(h, b) ==
  /\ b \in manifest[h]
  /\ countdown[b] > 0
  /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![h] = @ \ {b}]
  /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {b}
  /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED feed

PassAcross(g, h, b) ==
  /\ g # h
  /\ b \in manifest[g]
  /\ Cardinality(manifest[h]) < MaxLoad
  /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![g] = @ \ {b}, ![h] = @ \cup {b}]
  /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![b] = LeaseLen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feed, delivered>>

VoidStep == \E h \in Halls, b \in Bags : LeaseVoid(h, b)
DeliverStep == \E h \in Halls, b \in Bags : Deliver(h, b)

Next ==
  \/ TakeStep \/ VoidStep \/ DeliverStep \/ Tick
  \/ \E g, h \in Halls, b \in Bags : PassAcross(g, h, b)

  /\ SF_vars(TakeStep) /\ SF_vars(VoidStep) /\ SF_vars(DeliverStep)

CONSTANTS
  Bags = {g1, g2}
  Halls = {north, south}
  LeaseLen = 2
  MaxLoad = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT CustodyAccounted
PROPERTY AllBagsOut
nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags from one shared arrivals feed to the make-up carousels.
Two independent router instances -- the north hall and the south hall -- work the same feed.
Every bag in the building must be accounted for at every moment: it is either sitting on the
shared feed, on exactly one hall's custody manifest, or already delivered. A bag is never on
the feed and on a manifest at once, never on both halls' manifests, and never quietly
disappears.

A hall takes custody of a feed bag by opening a time-boxed custody lease on it: the bag comes
off the feed onto that hall's manifest with a fresh lease countdown. A shared conveyor clock
tick runs the countdown down on every outstanding lease. A hall may deliver a bag while its
lease still has time on it, which moves the bag from the hall's manifest to delivered. If a
lease's countdown reaches zero before delivery, the lease is void and the bag goes straight
back onto the shared feed, off the hall's manifest -- it is never left in limbo. A hall may
also pass a bag it holds directly across to the other hall, which moves the bag from one
manifest to the other in a single step and starts a fresh countdown.

The actions are: a hall opens a custody lease on a feed bag, the conveyor clock ticks the
outstanding countdowns down, a void lease returns its bag to the shared feed, a hall delivers
a bag whose lease is still live, and a hall passes a held bag across to the other hall.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared feed, the two halls' custody manifests, and the delivered bags
always partition the whole set of bags -- every bag is in exactly one of those places and
never on two manifests at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag is eventually delivered.

CONSTANTS Lanes, Robots, LaneCap, MaxRev

NoLane == "nolane"

VARIABLES level, rev, noteLane, noteRev, holding, slow

vars == <<level, rev, noteLane, noteRev, holding, slow>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ level \in [Lanes -> Nat]
  /\ rev \in [Lanes -> 0..MaxRev]
  /\ noteLane \in [Robots -> Lanes \cup {NoLane}]
  /\ noteRev \in [Robots -> 0..MaxRev]
  /\ holding \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ slow \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]

\* The whole point of the revision check: a lane is never filled past its cap,
\* not even by a deposit committed from an out-of-date read.
LaneNeverOverfull == \A l \in Lanes : level[l] <= LaneCap

Init ==
  /\ level = [l \in Lanes |-> 0]
  /\ rev = [l \in Lanes |-> 0]
  /\ noteLane = [r \in Robots |-> NoLane]
  /\ noteRev = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
  /\ holding = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
  /\ slow = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]

PickUp(r) ==
  /\ ~holding[r]
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<level, rev, noteLane, noteRev, slow>>

ReadLane(r, l) ==
  /\ holding[r] /\ ~slow[r]
  /\ noteLane[r] = NoLane
  /\ noteLane' = [noteLane EXCEPT ![r] = l]
  /\ noteRev' = [noteRev EXCEPT ![r] = rev[l]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<level, rev, holding, slow>>

\* Optimistic commit: the note must still match the lane's revision.
Deposit(r, l) ==
  /\ ~slow[r]
  /\ noteLane[r] = l
  /\ noteRev[r] = rev[l]
  /\ rev[l] < MaxRev
  /\ level[l] < LaneCap
  /\ level' = [level EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
  /\ noteLane' = [noteLane EXCEPT ![r] = NoLane]
  /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<noteRev, slow>>

Refused(r, l) ==
  /\ noteLane[r] = l
  /\ noteRev[r] # rev[l]
  /\ noteLane' = [noteLane EXCEPT ![r] = NoLane]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<level, rev, noteRev, holding, slow>>

DrawOff(l) ==
  /\ level[l] > 0
  /\ rev[l] < MaxRev
  /\ level' = [level EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
  /\ rev' = [rev EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<noteLane, noteRev, holding, slow>>

GoSlow(r) ==
  /\ ~slow[r]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<level, rev, noteLane, noteRev, holding>>

Resume(r) ==
  /\ slow[r]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<level, rev, noteLane, noteRev, holding>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : PickUp(r) \/ GoSlow(r) \/ Resume(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, l \in Lanes : ReadLane(r, l) \/ Deposit(r, l) \/ Refused(r, l)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : DrawOff(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Lanes = {ln1, ln2}
  Robots = {rb1, rb2}
  LaneCap = 2
  MaxRev = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT LaneNeverOverfull
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet feeds totes into the staging lanes of a pick station. Each lane holds
a limited number of totes and must never be overfilled -- an overfilled lane jams the station
and stops the whole aisle.

There is no lane lock. Robots work optimistically: a robot carrying a tote reads a lane,
taking a private note of the lane's identity and its current revision number, and later
tries to commit its deposit against that note. The commit only goes through if the lane's
revision is still the one the robot noted and the lane still has room; a successful deposit
adds the tote and advances the lane's revision. If another robot got there first the
revision has moved on, the commit is refused, and the robot throws its note away and retries
from scratch. The pick station also draws totes off a lane, which likewise advances that
lane's revision. Lane revisions advance only up to a bounded number of times in the window
modelled here.

Robots can be slow but they never fail. A slow robot is still running its path planner: it
neither reads a lane nor commits while it is slow, so its outstanding note simply ages and
is very likely to be refused when it finally tries. Slow robots resume at any time.

The actions are: a free robot picks up a tote, a running robot reads a lane and notes its
revision, a running robot commits its deposit when the revision still matches and the lane
has room, a robot whose noted revision is out of date discards the note and retries, the
pick station draws a tote off a lane, a robot becomes slow, and a slow robot resumes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No staging lane ever holds more totes than its capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od3m5p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, Desks, Quorum

Nobody == "nobody"
NoDesk == "nodesk"

VARIABLES state, tally, grant, at, inService

vars == <<state, tally, grant, at, inService>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ state \in [Members -> {"idle", "waiting", "posting", "done"}]
  /\ tally \in [Members -> SUBSET Members]
  /\ grant \in [Desks -> Members \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ at \in [Members -> Desks \cup {NoDesk}]
  /\ inService \subseteq Desks

\* Exclusion is carried by the grant register: whoever is posting must be the
\* bank the desk's register names, and a register names one bank.
DeskExclusive ==
  \A m \in Members :
    state[m] = "posting" => (at[m] \in Desks /\ grant[at[m]] = m)

Init ==
  /\ state = [m \in Members |-> "idle"]
  /\ tally = [m \in Members |-> {}]
  /\ grant = [d \in Desks |-> Nobody]
  /\ at = [m \in Members |-> NoDesk]
  /\ inService = Desks

Request(m) ==
  /\ state[m] = "idle"
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![m] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, grant, at, inService>>

Vote(v, m) ==
  /\ state[m] = "waiting"
  /\ v \notin tally[m]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![m] = @ \cup {v}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, grant, at, inService>>

Grant(m, d) ==
  /\ state[m] = "waiting"
  /\ Cardinality(tally[m]) >= Quorum
  /\ d \in inService
  /\ grant[d] = Nobody
  /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![d] = m]
  /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![m] = d]
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![m] = "posting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, inService>>

Release(m) ==
  /\ state[m] = "posting"
  /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![at[m]] = Nobody]
  /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![m] = NoDesk]
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![m] = "done"]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![m] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED inService

\* Runtime capacity change; the last desk in service is never withdrawn.
Withdraw(d) ==
  /\ d \in inService
  /\ grant[d] = Nobody
  /\ Cardinality(inService) > 1
  /\ inService' = inService \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, tally, grant, at>>

Reinstate(d) ==
  /\ d \notin inService
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, tally, grant, at>>

VoteStep == \E v \in Members, m \in Members : Vote(v, m)
GrantStep == \E m \in Members, d \in Desks : Grant(m, d)
ReleaseStep == \E m \in Members : Release(m)

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Members : Request(m) \/ Release(m)
  \/ VoteStep \/ GrantStep
  \/ \E d \in Desks : Withdraw(d) \/ Reinstate(d)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(VoteStep) /\ SF_vars(GrantStep) /\ SF_vars(ReleaseStep)

DeskGranted ==
  \A m \in Members : (state[m] = "waiting") ~> (state[m] \in {"posting", "done"})
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Members = {mA, mB}
  Desks = {dk1, dk2}
  Quorum = 2

INVARIANT DeskExclusive
PROPERTY DeskGranted
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is posted through the clearing house's posting desks.
A desk is a critical resource: while one member bank is posting its batch at a desk, no
other bank may be posting at that same desk, or the two batches would interleave on the
central book.

Access is decided by the members themselves. A bank that wants to post raises a request, and
the other members vote on it; the clearing house grants a desk to a requesting bank only
once a quorum of distinct members has voted for that request. The grant is written into the
desk's grant register and the bank starts posting; when the bank is finished it releases the
desk, the register entry is cleared, and the bank's tally is wiped. Each member posts one
batch per clearing window, so a bank that has finished does not request again.

The number of desks in service changes during the window: the clearing house takes an idle
desk out of service for reconciliation and brings desks back later, but it never takes the
last desk in service out, so there is always at least one desk available.

The actions are: a member raises a posting request, a member votes for another member's
request, the clearing house grants an in-service free desk to a request that has reached
quorum, a posting bank finishes and releases its desk, take an idle desk out of service, and
return a desk to service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bank that is posting is always named in the grant register of the very
desk it is posting at, so two banks can never be posting at the same desk.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bank that raises a posting request eventually gets a desk and posts.

---- MODULE W4Od16m9p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Scripts, Bins, Staff, MaxEpoch

Cert == [rx: Scripts, bin: Bins, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]

VARIABLES epoch, view, journal, slow, pickedUp

vars == <<epoch, view, journal, slow, pickedUp>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ view \in [Staff -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ journal \subseteq Cert
  /\ slow \in [Staff -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ pickedUp \subseteq Scripts

HasBinNow(r) == \E c \in journal : c.rx = r /\ c.ep = epoch
BinTakenNow(b) == \E c \in journal : c.bin = b /\ c.ep = epoch

\* Within one rack configuration a bin belongs to one prescription; across
\* epochs the journal keeps the old certificates as history.
BinAgreement ==
  \A c1, c2 \in journal :
    (c1.bin = c2.bin /\ c1.ep = c2.ep) => c1.rx = c2.rx

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ view = [s \in Staff |-> 0]
  /\ journal = {}
  /\ slow = [s \in Staff |-> FALSE]
  /\ pickedUp = {}

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, journal, slow, pickedUp>>

RefreshView(s) ==
  /\ ~slow[s]
  /\ view[s] # epoch
  /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, journal, slow, pickedUp>>

\* A stale view cannot assign: that is what fences off a lagging bench.
Assign(s, r, b) ==
  /\ ~slow[s]
  /\ view[s] = epoch
  /\ r \notin pickedUp
  /\ ~HasBinNow(r)
  /\ ~BinTakenNow(b)
  /\ journal' = journal \cup {[rx |-> r, bin |-> b, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, slow, pickedUp>>

Collect(r) ==
  /\ HasBinNow(r)
  /\ r \notin pickedUp
  /\ pickedUp' = pickedUp \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, journal, slow>>

FallBehind(s) ==
  /\ ~slow[s]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, journal, pickedUp>>

Resume(s) ==
  /\ slow[s]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, journal, pickedUp>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E s \in Staff : RefreshView(s) \/ FallBehind(s) \/ Resume(s)
  \/ \E s \in Staff, r \in Scripts, b \in Bins : Assign(s, r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Scripts : Collect(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====
nl:
A pharmacy's prescription dispenser sorts filled prescriptions into pickup bins. Two bins
are in the rack, and within one rack configuration a bin belongs to exactly one
prescription: assigning the same bin to two prescriptions in the same configuration would
send a patient home with someone else's medicine.

The rack is reconfigured from time to time -- trays are swapped and the bins are emptied and
re-labelled -- and each reconfiguration bumps a configuration epoch. Every assignment the
dispenser makes is written to the audit journal as a certificate carrying the prescription,
the bin, and the epoch it was made under. After a bump, a prescription that has not been
picked up must be assigned a bin again under the new epoch, and the old certificate stays in
the journal as history.

Dispensing staff each carry a view of the current epoch. A staff member may only assign a
bin while their view matches the dispenser's current epoch, the prescription has not already
been assigned a bin in this epoch, and no other prescription holds that bin in this epoch. A
staff member can be slow but never fails: a slow member is mid-count at the bench, does not
refresh their epoch view and does not assign bins, so their view falls behind; they catch up
when they resume. A prescription that has been picked up is finished and is never assigned a
bin again.

The actions are: reconfigure the rack and bump the epoch, a running staff member refreshes
their epoch view, a running staff member with a current view assigns a free bin to a
prescription and writes the certificate, a patient picks up a prescription assigned in the
current epoch, a staff member becomes slow, and a slow staff member resumes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any two audit certificates that name the same bin under the same
configuration epoch also name the same prescription, so a bin is never allocated twice
within one configuration.

---- MODULE W4Od2m2p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, MaxRound

VARIABLES round, phase, acked, fired, firedRound, slow

vars == <<round, phase, acked, fired, firedRound, slow>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "preparing", "committed"}
  /\ acked \subseteq Robots
  /\ fired \in BOOLEAN
  /\ firedRound \in 0..MaxRound
  /\ slow \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]

\* The irreversible discharge freezes the protocol on the round that authorised
\* it: no later round exists, so there is no path to a second discharge.
FrozenAfterFiring ==
  fired => (phase = "committed" /\ firedRound = round)

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ fired = FALSE
  /\ firedRound = 0
  /\ slow = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]

OpenRound ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ ~fired
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ phase' = "preparing"
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fired, firedRound, slow>>

Prepared(r) ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ ~slow[r]
  /\ r \notin acked
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, fired, firedRound, slow>>

\* The commit point: fires once, stamps the round, and stops the protocol.
CommitFire ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ acked = Robots
  /\ fired' = TRUE
  /\ firedRound' = round
  /\ phase' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, acked, slow>>

AbandonRound ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ acked # Robots
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, fired, firedRound, slow>>

FallBehind(r) ==
  /\ ~slow[r]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, acked, fired, firedRound>>

Resume(r) ==
  /\ slow[r]
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, acked, fired, firedRound>>

PrepareStep == \E r \in Robots : Prepared(r)
ResumeStep == \E r \in Robots : Resume(r)

Next ==
  \/ OpenRound \/ CommitFire \/ AbandonRound \/ PrepareStep
  \/ \E r \in Robots : FallBehind(r) \/ Resume(r)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(CommitFire) /\ WF_vars(PrepareStep) /\ WF_vars(ResumeStep)

DischargeHappens == (phase = "preparing" /\ acked = Robots) ~> fired
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Robots = {rb1, rb2}
  MaxRound = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT FrozenAfterFiring
PROPERTY DischargeHappens
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet guards a high-bay aisle fitted with a one-shot foam suppression
canister. Firing the canister is irreversible: the foam is gone, the aisle is out of use
until it is re-charged by hand, and the fleet must never be able to fire it a second time.

The fleet controller runs the discharge as a two-phase commit with the robots working the
aisle. It opens a numbered round and asks every robot to prepare, which means clearing the
aisle and acknowledging. Each robot acknowledges the open round on its own. If the
controller gives up while an acknowledgement is still missing, the round is abandoned and
the controller returns to idle, free to open a later, higher-numbered round -- but only a
bounded number of rounds fit in the window modelled here. When every robot has acknowledged
the open round, the controller commits: the canister fires, the firing is stamped with the
number of the round that authorised it, and the protocol is frozen there. No new round can
be opened once the canister has fired.

Robots can be slow but never fail. A slow robot is still driving out of the aisle and will
not acknowledge; it resumes later and then acknowledges normally. Slowness is what makes the
controller abandon a round.

The actions are: open a new numbered round and ask for prepares, a running robot
acknowledges the open round, commit and fire the canister once every robot has acknowledged,
abandon a round that is still missing an acknowledgement, a robot becomes slow, and a slow
robot resumes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: If the canister has fired, the controller's round number is still exactly
the round stamped on the firing and the protocol sits in its committed state, so no further
round can ever be opened and no second discharge can occur.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Once every robot has acknowledged the open round, the canister eventually
fires.

---- MODULE W4Od19m2p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Titles, Branches, Patrons, ShelfCap, MaxOverride

NoPatron == "nopatron"

VARIABLES status, votes, holdFor, budget, forced

vars == <<status, votes, holdFor, budget, forced>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ status \in [Titles -> {"none", "prepared", "onshelf"}]
  /\ votes \in [Titles -> SUBSET Branches]
  /\ holdFor \in [Titles -> Patrons \cup {NoPatron}]
  /\ budget \in 0..MaxOverride
  /\ forced \subseteq Titles

\* A prepared reservation escrows its shelf slot, so escrowed and shelved
\* titles together are what the shelf limit applies to.
Escrowed == {t \in Titles : status[t] \in {"prepared", "onshelf"}}

ShelfWithinLimit == Cardinality(Escrowed) <= ShelfCap

Init ==
  /\ status = [t \in Titles |-> "none"]
  /\ votes = [t \in Titles |-> {}]
  /\ holdFor = [t \in Titles |-> NoPatron]
  /\ budget = MaxOverride
  /\ forced = {}

Request(p, t) ==
  /\ status[t] = "none"
  /\ Cardinality(Escrowed) < ShelfCap
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
  /\ holdFor' = [holdFor EXCEPT ![t] = p]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<budget, forced>>

BranchVote(b, t) ==
  /\ status[t] = "prepared"
  /\ b \notin votes[t]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {b}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, holdFor, budget, forced>>

CommitHold(t) ==
  /\ status[t] = "prepared"
  /\ votes[t] = Branches
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "onshelf"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, holdFor, budget, forced>>

\* The override skips the branch votes; the slot was escrowed already.
Override(t) ==
  /\ status[t] = "prepared"
  /\ budget > 0
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "onshelf"]
  /\ budget' = budget - 1
  /\ forced' = forced \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, holdFor>>

AbortHold(t) ==
  /\ status[t] = "prepared"
  /\ votes[t] # Branches
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ holdFor' = [holdFor EXCEPT ![t] = NoPatron]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<budget, forced>>

Collect(t) ==
  /\ status[t] = "onshelf"
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ holdFor' = [holdFor EXCEPT ![t] = NoPatron]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<budget, forced>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Patrons, t \in Titles : Request(p, t)
  \/ \E b \in Branches, t \in Titles : BranchVote(b, t)
  \/ \E t \in Titles : CommitHold(t) \/ Override(t) \/ AbortHold(t) \/ Collect(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====
nl:
A library branch keeps a hold shelf behind the desk for reserved books. The shelf has a hard
physical limit: the number of books either already sitting on it or promised to it by an
in-flight reservation must never exceed the number of slots it has.

A reservation is set up as a two-phase commit across the library's branches. When a patron
asks for a title, the desk takes a shelf slot into escrow and puts the reservation into the
prepared phase, recording which patron it is for; the escrowed slot counts against the
shelf's limit from that moment, before the book has physically arrived. Each branch then
votes on the prepared reservation. Once every branch has voted, the reservation commits and
the book goes onto the shelf. If a vote is still outstanding, the desk may abort the
reservation instead, which gives the escrowed slot back.

The head librarian has a privileged override and may push a prepared reservation through to
the shelf without waiting for the branch votes; the override budget for the day is limited
and each use spends one. The override skips the consensus, never the shelf limit -- the slot
was already escrowed when the reservation was prepared. When the patron collects the book,
the slot is freed and the title can be reserved again.

The actions are: a patron requests a title, which escrows a shelf slot and prepares the
reservation; a branch votes on a prepared reservation; commit a reservation whose votes are
all in; the head librarian spends one override to push a prepared reservation onto the shelf;
abort a prepared reservation that is still missing a vote and release its slot; and a patron
collects a book from the shelf, freeing the slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of titles that are either on the hold shelf or escrowed by a
prepared reservation never exceeds the shelf's slot count.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks

Free == "free"
NoBlock == "noblock"
MaxSerial == Cardinality(Trains)

VARIABLES owner, serial, authority, inBlock, inService, arrived

vars == <<owner, serial, authority, inBlock, inService, arrived>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ owner \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {Free}]
  /\ serial \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxSerial]
  /\ authority \in [Trains -> 0..MaxSerial]
  /\ inBlock \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]
  /\ inService \subseteq Blocks
  /\ arrived \subseteq Trains

\* Exclusion rests on the register: an occupant must be the named owner and its
\* authority stamp must still match the block's serial.
ExclusiveOccupancy ==
  \A t \in Trains :
    inBlock[t] # NoBlock =>
      /\ owner[inBlock[t]] = t
      /\ authority[t] = serial[inBlock[t]]

Init ==
  /\ owner = [b \in Blocks |-> Free]
  /\ serial = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ authority = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ inBlock = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ inService = Blocks
  /\ arrived = {}

\* The compare-and-swap: Free is exchanged for the train, serial advances.
SwapIn(t, b) ==
  /\ t \notin arrived
  /\ inBlock[t] = NoBlock
  /\ b \in inService
  /\ owner[b] = Free
  /\ serial[b] < MaxSerial
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ serial' = [serial EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ authority' = [authority EXCEPT ![t] = serial[b] + 1]
  /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inService, arrived>>

Release(t) ==
  /\ inBlock[t] # NoBlock
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![inBlock[t]] = Free]
  /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ authority' = [authority EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ arrived' = arrived \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<serial, inService>>

TakeOut(b) ==
  /\ b \in inService
  /\ owner[b] = Free
  /\ Cardinality(inService) > 1
  /\ inService' = inService \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, serial, authority, inBlock, arrived>>

PutBack(b) ==

nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks. A block is a critical resource: at most one
train may be inside a given block at a time, or the two trains are on a collision course.

Each block has a compare-and-swap occupancy register holding the current occupant, or Free,
together with a serial number. A train enters a block by swapping Free for its own identity;
the same swap advances the block's serial and hands the train a movement authority stamped
with that new serial. A train inside a block leaves it by putting the register back to Free
and surrendering its authority. Each train in this window makes one trip: it waits, occupies
one block, and then has arrived.

The number of blocks in service changes during operation. Control may take an empty block
out of service for track work and put it back later, but it never takes out the last block
in service, so a waiting train always has somewhere to go.

The actions are: a waiting train swaps itself into a free in-service block and takes the
stamped authority, an occupying train releases its block back to Free and has arrived, take
an empty in-service block out of service, and return a block to service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every train that is inside a block is the occupant named in that block's
register and holds an authority whose stamp equals the register's current serial, so two
trains can never be inside the same block.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every waiting train eventually occupies a block.

  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ flagged' = {r \in Runways : assignedBy[r] # Nobody}

ReadRegister(c) ==
  /\ handle[c] # gen
  /\ handle' = [handle EXCEPT ![c] = gen]

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Runways = {rw27, rw09}
  Consoles = {conA, conB}
  MaxGen = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT NoStaleWriteStanding
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator is driven by two independent console instances that share one
pool of runway assignments. The pool sits behind a compare-and-swap register that carries a
generation number, and each console holds its own handle on that generation.

The supervisor bumps the generation whenever the airport configuration changes -- a runway
direction flip, a new noise regime. A bump immediately marks every existing assignment in the
shared pool as needing re-affirmation, because an assignment made under the old configuration
means nothing under the new one. A console picks up the new generation by re-reading the
register into its handle.

A console writes to the pool by stamping the assignment with the generation its own handle
carries. It may take a free runway and assign it, re-affirm an assignment of its own that is
waiting for re-affirmation, or withdraw one of its own assignments and return the runway to
the pool. Every one of those writes is only accepted while the console's handle equals the
register's generation; a console that has not picked up the latest generation is stale and
its writes are refused. That refusal is the entire safety mechanism, since either console can
touch any runway in the shared pool.

The actions are: the supervisor bumps the generation and flags every assignment for
re-affirmation, a console re-reads the register into its handle, a console with a current
handle assigns a free runway, a console with a current handle re-affirms its own flagged
assignment, and a console with a current handle withdraws its own assignment.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every assignment in the shared pool that is not flagged for re-affirmation
carries the register's current generation stamp, so no stale console's write is ever standing
in the pool as valid.

CONSTANTS Batches, Gateways, MaxVer

NoBatch == "nobatch"

VARIABLES version, released, snapBatch, snapVer, up

vars == <<version, released, snapBatch, snapVer, up>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in [Batches -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ released \subseteq Batches
  /\ snapBatch \in [Gateways -> Batches \cup {NoBatch}]
  /\ snapVer \in [Gateways -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ up \in [Gateways -> BOOLEAN]

\* A snapshot that still matches its batch is a live authorisation to act. If
\* the batch were already released, that authorisation would be a second one.
NoLiveAuthAfterRelease ==
  \A g \in Gateways :
    (snapBatch[g] # NoBatch /\ snapVer[g] = version[snapBatch[g]])
      => snapBatch[g] \notin released

Init ==
  /\ version = [b \in Batches |-> 0]
  /\ released = {}
  /\ snapBatch = [g \in Gateways |-> NoBatch]
  /\ snapVer = [g \in Gateways |-> 0]
  /\ up = [g \in Gateways |-> TRUE]

Snapshot(g, b) ==
  /\ up[g]
  /\ snapBatch[g] = NoBatch
  /\ b \notin released
  /\ snapBatch' = [snapBatch EXCEPT ![g] = b]
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![g] = version[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, released, up>>

\* Releasing advances the version, which invalidates every rival snapshot.
Release(g, b) ==
  /\ up[g]
  /\ snapBatch[g] = b
  /\ snapVer[g] = version[b]
  /\ b \notin released
  /\ version[b] < MaxVer
  /\ released' = released \cup {b}
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ snapBatch' = [snapBatch EXCEPT ![g] = NoBatch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVer, up>>

Amend(g, b) ==
  /\ up[g]
  /\ snapBatch[g] = b
  /\ snapVer[g] = version[b]
  /\ version[b] + 1 < MaxVer
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ snapBatch' = [snapBatch EXCEPT ![g] = NoBatch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<released, snapVer, up>>

Discard(g) ==
  /\ snapBatch[g] # NoBatch
  /\ snapVer[g] # version[snapBatch[g]]
  /\ snapBatch' = [snapBatch EXCEPT ![g] = NoBatch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, released, snapVer, up>>

CrashSilently(g) ==
  /\ up[g]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![g] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, released, snapBatch, snapVer>>

ComeBack(g) ==
  /\ ~up[g]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![g] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, released, snapBatch, snapVer>>

SnapStep == \E g \in Gateways, b \in Batches : Snapshot(g, b)
ReleaseStep == \E g \in Gateways, b \in Batches : Release(g, b)
DiscardStep == \E g \in Gateways : Discard(g)
BackStep == \E g \in Gateways : ComeBack(g)

Next ==
  \/ SnapStep \/ ReleaseStep \/ DiscardStep \/ BackStep
  \/ \E g \in Gateways, b \in Batches : Amend(g, b)
  \/ \E g \in Gateways : CrashSilently(g)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(SnapStep) /\ SF_vars(ReleaseStep)
  /\ SF_vars(DiscardStep) /\ SF_vars(BackStep)

AllReleased == \A b \in Batches : <>(b \in released)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Batches = {pb1, pb2}
  Gateways = {gw1, gw2}
  MaxVer = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT NoLiveAuthAfterRelease
PROPERTY AllReleased
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement runs payment batches. Releasing a batch to the settlement
network is irreversible -- the funds leave and cannot be recalled -- so a batch must be
released at most once, even though several gateway processes may be working on it at the
same time.

There is no lock on a batch. Each batch record carries a version number and the gateways work
optimistically. A gateway takes a snapshot of one unreleased batch, recording the batch and
the version it saw. Later it may act on that snapshot, but only while the batch's version is
still the version in the snapshot. Acting means one of two things: releasing the batch, which
marks it released and advances its version, or amending it, which just advances its version.
Either way the version moves, which is precisely what makes every other outstanding snapshot
of that batch worthless. A gateway that notices its snapshot no longer matches the batch's
version throws it away and starts over. A batch's version can only be advanced a bounded
number of times in the window modelled here, and amendments stop early enough to leave room
for the release.

A gateway can crash silently: it stops with no notice and keeps whatever snapshot it was
holding, so it may come back up carrying a snapshot from before the outage. A crashed gateway
neither snapshots nor acts.

The actions are: a live gateway snapshots an unreleased batch, a live gateway releases a
batch whose version still matches its snapshot, a live gateway amends a batch whose version
still matches its snapshot, a gateway discards a snapshot whose version no longer matches,
a gateway crashes silently while keeping its snapshot, and a crashed gateway comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any outstanding snapshot whose version still matches its batch belongs to a
batch that has not been released, so no second release can ever be authorised.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every batch is eventually released.

CONSTANTS Servers, Outcomes, Quorum

NoVal == "noval"

VARIABLES tabled, vote, sealed, ladder, up

vars == <<tabled, vote, sealed, ladder, up>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ tabled \subseteq Outcomes
  /\ vote \in [Servers -> Outcomes \cup {NoVal}]
  /\ sealed \in [Servers -> Outcomes \cup {NoVal}]
  /\ ladder \in Outcomes \cup {NoVal}
  /\ up \in [Servers -> BOOLEAN]

Backing(v) == Cardinality({s \in Servers : vote[s] = v})

\* A server votes once and never revotes, so with a strict-majority quorum only
\* one outcome can ever be backed; the ladder therefore cannot be contradicted.
LadderUncontradicted == \A s \in Servers : sealed[s] # NoVal => ladder = sealed[s]

Init ==
  /\ tabled = {}
  /\ vote = [s \in Servers |-> NoVal]
  /\ sealed = [s \in Servers |-> NoVal]
  /\ ladder = NoVal
  /\ up = [s \in Servers |-> TRUE]

Report(v) ==
  /\ v \notin tabled
  /\ tabled' = tabled \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, sealed, ladder, up>>

CastVote(s, v) ==
  /\ up[s]
  /\ v \in tabled
  /\ vote[s] = NoVal
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![s] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tabled, sealed, ladder, up>>

\* The seal is a blind last-writer-wins write to the ladder; safety comes from
\* the quorum, not from re-checking what is already there.
Seal(s, v) ==
  /\ up[s]
  /\ sealed[s] = NoVal
  /\ Backing(v) >= Quorum
  /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![s] = v]
  /\ ladder' = v
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tabled, vote, up>>

CrashSilently(s) ==
  /\ up[s]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tabled, vote, sealed, ladder>>

ComeBack(s) ==
  /\ ~up[s]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tabled, vote, sealed, ladder>>

Next ==
  \/ \E v \in Outcomes : Report(v)
  \/ \E s \in Servers, v \in Outcomes : CastVote(s, v) \/ Seal(s, v)
  \/ \E s \in Servers : CrashSilently(s) \/ ComeBack(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Servers = {lb1, lb2, lb3}
  Outcomes = {teamA, teamB}
  Quorum = 2

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT LadderUncontradicted
nl:
A multiplayer game's lobby matchmaker has to seal the outcome of a finished match onto the
season ladder. Sealing is irreversible: the ladder entry is permanent, it feeds payouts and
rank decay, and support cannot undo it. The lobby must therefore seal one outcome and only
one, even though the clients disagree about who won.

The lobby runs on three servers. Client reports put candidate outcomes on the table -- team A
won, or team B won. Each server picks at most one of the tabled outcomes and votes for it,
and a server never changes its vote afterwards, not even across a restart. A server may seal
an outcome once it can see that a quorum of servers has voted for that same outcome; sealing
records the outcome in the server's own durable record and writes it to the season ladder
entry. Because a server votes once and a quorum is a strict majority of the three servers,
two different outcomes can never both collect a quorum.

A server can crash silently: it stops with no announcement, and the other servers keep going
on the quorum they can still assemble. A crashed server's vote and sealed record are durable
and survive the outage; it may come back up later and carry on.

The actions are: a client report puts a candidate outcome on the table, a live server votes
for a tabled outcome, a live server seals a quorum-backed outcome into its own record and
onto the ladder, a server crashes silently, and a crashed server comes back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every server that has sealed an outcome has sealed exactly the outcome
standing on the season ladder, so the ladder is never overwritten with a second, different
result.

SnapVal(c) == snap[c].val
