  /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ snap \in [Cars -> [ver: -1..MaxVer, val: SUBSET Floors]]
  /\ served \subseteq Floors
  /\ acked \subseteq Floors
  /\ up \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]

\* Nothing acknowledged may fall out of the world: a stale write-back that
\* re-installed an old board would strand a call in neither place.
NoCallLost == acked \subseteq (board \cup served)

  /\ ver = 0
  /\ snap = [c \in Cars |-> NoSnap]
  /\ served = {}
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ up = [c \in Cars |-> TRUE]

  /\ ~HoldsSnap(c)
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = [ver |-> ver, val |-> board]]

  /\ ver < MaxVer
  /\ f \notin SnapVal(c)
  /\ f \notin served

  /\ ver' = ver + 1
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {f}
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]

  /\ SnapVer(c) = ver
  /\ ver < MaxVer
  /\ f \in SnapVal(c)

  /\ ver' = ver + 1
  /\ served' = served \cup {f}
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, up>>

  /\ SnapVer(c) # ver

  /\ up[c]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, ver, snap, served, acked>>

ComeBack(c) ==

  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Floors = {fl3, fl7}
  Cars = {car1, car2}
  MaxVer = 4

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE

INVARIANT NoCallLost
PROPERTY CallsServed
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper keeps one shared hall-call board: the set of floors with an
outstanding hall call. Several car controllers update that board, and they do it through a
compare-and-swap register holding the board contents together with a version number.

A controller first reads the register, keeping a private snapshot of the version it saw and
the board contents it saw. It then writes back a modified copy of its own snapshot, and the
write only lands while the register's version is still the version in the snapshot; a
successful write advances the version and clears the snapshot. There are two kinds of write:
registering a new hall call, which adds the floor to the snapshot copy and acknowledges the
call to the waiting passenger, and completing a call, which removes the floor from the
snapshot copy and records the floor as served. A controller whose snapshot version has been
overtaken has its write refused and drops the snapshot. A call that has been served is never
registered again, and the register only takes a bounded number of successful writes in the
window modelled here.

A controller can crash silently: it stops with no announcement while keeping its snapshot,
and it may come back up later still holding it. A crashed controller neither reads nor
writes. The version check is what stops a stale write-back from re-installing an old board
and wiping out a call another controller had already registered.

The actions are: a live controller reads the register into its snapshot, a live controller's
write registers and acknowledges a new hall call, a live controller's write completes a call
and records it served, a controller with an overtaken snapshot has its write refused, a
controller crashes silently while keeping its snapshot, and a crashed controller comes back
up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every hall call that has been acknowledged to a passenger is still either
outstanding on the shared board or recorded as served, so no acknowledged call is ever lost
by a write-back.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every acknowledged hall call is eventually served.

Held(S) ==

  /\ issued \in 0..Stock
  /\ atDoor \in [Doors -> 0..MaxCap]
  /\ cap \in [Doors -> 1..MaxCap]
  /\ houseClaim \in BOOLEAN
  /\ doorClaim \in [Doors -> BOOLEAN]

\* vault holds whatever is left of the fixed stock.

  /\ vault = Stock
  /\ issued = 0
  /\ atDoor = [d \in Doors |-> 0]
  /\ cap = [d \in Doors |-> 1]
  /\ houseClaim = FALSE
  /\ doorClaim = [d \in Doors |-> FALSE]

TakeHouse ==
  /\ ~houseClaim
  /\ houseClaim' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, issued, atDoor, cap, doorClaim>>

\* Coarse before fine: no door claim without the house claim.
TakeDoor(d) ==

  /\ ~doorClaim[d]

  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, issued, atDoor, cap, houseClaim>>

  /\ vault > 0
  /\ atDoor[d] < cap[d]
  /\ vault' = vault - 1
  /\ atDoor' = [atDoor EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
  /\ issued' = issued + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, houseClaim, doorClaim>>

  /\ atDoor[d] > 0
  /\ vault' = vault + 1
  /\ atDoor' = [atDoor EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
  /\ issued' = issued - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, houseClaim, doorClaim>>

\* Runtime re-provisioning of a keypad's capacity, never below what it holds.
SetCap(d, n) ==

  /\ n >= atDoor[d]
  /\ n # cap[d]
  /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![d] = n]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, issued, atDoor, houseClaim, doorClaim>>

  /\ doorClaim[d]
  /\ doorClaim' = [doorClaim EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, issued, atDoor, cap, houseClaim>>

  /\ \A d \in Doors : ~doorClaim[d]
  /\ houseClaim' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, issued, atDoor, cap, doorClaim>>

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Doors = {frontDoor, backDoor}
  Stock = 2
  MaxCap = 2

INVARIANT CredentialsBalance
nl:
A smart-home door lock network hands out a fixed stock of digital guest credentials. The
stock never grows and never shrinks: every credential is at all times either sitting unissued
in the hub's vault or provisioned into exactly one door's keypad. The hub also keeps a
running summary of how many credentials it has issued in total, and that summary must always
agree with what the doors actually hold added up.

Changing a door's credentials is done under two claims taken in order, coarse then fine: the
hub first takes the house-wide administration claim, and only while holding it may it take
the claim on an individual door. Provisioning moves one credential out of the vault into that
door's keypad and adds one to the hub summary; revoking moves one back out of the keypad into
the vault and takes one off the summary. The door claim is dropped when the work on that door
is finished, and the house-wide claim is only dropped once no door claim is outstanding.

A door's keypad capacity is re-provisioned at runtime while its door claim is held -- the
installer can set it to any value up to the model's maximum -- but it can never be set below
the number of credentials that door is already holding.

The actions are: take the house-wide administration claim, take an individual door's claim
while holding the house-wide one, provision a credential from the vault into a claimed door,
revoke a credential from a claimed door back into the vault, set a claimed door's capacity to
a new value not below what it holds, drop a door's claim, and drop the house-wide claim once
no door claim is outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The hub's issued summary always equals the total credentials actually held
across all the doors, and that summary plus the vault always equals the fixed stock, so no
credential is ever conjured up or lost.

EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxLog

Vacant == "vacant"
Nobody == "nobody"

VARIABLES coord, up, phase, holder, log

vars == <<coord, up, phase, holder, log>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coord \in Nodes \cup {Vacant}
  /\ up \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ phase \in [Nodes -> {"idle", "waiting", "in", "done"}]
  /\ holder \in Nodes \cup {Nobody}
  /\ log \in Seq([who: Nodes, ev: {"open", "close"}])

\* A correct console run alternates open and close; two opens in a row would be
\* exactly the overlap the console must never allow.
LogAlternates ==
  \A i \in 1..Len(log) : (i + 1 <= Len(log)) => log[i].ev # log[i + 1].ev

CoordDown == IF coord \in Nodes THEN ~up[coord] ELSE TRUE

Init ==
  /\ coord = Vacant
  /\ up = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
  /\ phase = [n \in Nodes |-> "idle"]
  /\ holder = Nobody
  /\ log = <<>>

Elect(n) ==
  /\ coord = Vacant /\ up[n]
  /\ coord' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, phase, holder, log>>

CrashSilently(n) ==
  /\ up[n]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, phase, holder, log>>

NoticeCoord ==
  /\ coord # Vacant /\ CoordDown
  /\ coord' = Vacant
  /\ UNCHANGED <<up, phase, holder, log>>

Restart(n) ==
  /\ ~up[n]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, phase, holder, log>>

AskConsole(n) ==
  /\ phase[n] = "idle"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![n] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, up, holder, log>>

OpenSession(n) ==
  /\ coord # Vacant /\ ~CoordDown
  /\ phase[n] = "waiting"
  /\ holder = Nobody
  /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
  /\ holder' = n
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![n] = "in"]
  /\ log' = Append(log, [who |-> n, ev |-> "open"])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, up>>

CloseSession(n) ==
  /\ holder = n /\ up[n]
  /\ holder' = Nobody
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![n] = "done"]
  /\ log' = Append(log, [who |-> n, ev |-> "close"])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, up>>

\* Fencing a silently dead holder: the session is closed on its behalf.
ForceClose(n) ==
  /\ holder = n /\ ~up[n]
  /\ holder' = Nobody
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![n] = "done"]
  /\ log' = Append(log, [who |-> n, ev |-> "close"])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, up>>

ElectStep == \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
RestartStep == \E n \in Nodes : Restart(n)
OpenStep == \E n \in Nodes : OpenSession(n)
CloseStep == \E n \in Nodes : CloseSession(n) \/ ForceClose(n)

Next ==
  \/ ElectStep \/ NoticeCoord \/ RestartStep \/ OpenStep \/ CloseStep
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : CrashSilently(n) \/ AskConsole(n)

Spec ==
  /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(ElectStep) /\ SF_vars(RestartStep) /\ SF_vars(NoticeCoord)
  /\ SF_vars(OpenStep) /\ SF_vars(CloseStep)

ConsoleGranted ==
  \A n \in Nodes : (phase[n] = "waiting") ~> (phase[n] \in {"in", "done"})
====

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards one stock-adjustment console. The console is a critical
resource: while one branch node has an adjustment session open on it, no other node may open
a session, or two nodes would be re-counting the same fridge at once and the unit counts
would come out wrong.

The branch nodes elect a coordinator, and only the live coordinator may open a session for a
waiting node. Every session boundary is written to the console's audit log as an entry saying
which node it was and whether the session opened or closed, so a correct run of the console
shows the log strictly alternating: open, close, open, close.

A node can crash silently -- it stops with no announcement. The coordinator pointer is not
cleared by the crash itself; the bank notices separately that the coordinator is down and
vacates the pointer so a live node can be elected. If the crashed node was the one holding
the console, the session is force-closed on its behalf, which writes the closing entry to the
log and frees the console. A crashed node can be restarted. Each node needs the console once
per shift, so a node that has had its session does not ask again.

The actions are: elect a live node as coordinator, a node crashes silently, the bank notices
a dead coordinator and vacates the pointer, restart a crashed node, a node asks for the
console, the live coordinator opens a session for a waiting node when the console is free, a
node with a session closes it, and a crashed session-holder's session is force-closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The console's audit log never has two entries of the same kind next to each
other, so no session is ever opened while another is still open.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every node that asks for the console eventually gets its session.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Centres, Trains, Quorum, MaxOverride

Nobody == "nobody"
NoSlot == "noslot"

VARIABLES freeList, allocTo, want, tally, budget

vars == <<freeList, allocTo, want, tally, budget>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ freeList \subseteq Slots
  /\ allocTo \in [Slots -> Trains \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ want \in [Trains -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ tally \in [Trains -> SUBSET Centres]
  /\ budget \in 0..MaxOverride

\* The free list and the allocation table are two views of one truth; a slot
\* left on the free list after being handed out is a double allocation waiting
\* to happen.
BooksComplement == \A s \in Slots : (s \in freeList) <=> (allocTo[s] = Nobody)

Init ==
  /\ freeList = Slots
  /\ allocTo = [s \in Slots |-> Nobody]
  /\ want = [t \in Trains |-> NoSlot]
  /\ tally = [t \in Trains |-> {}]
  /\ budget = MaxOverride

AskFor(t, s) ==
  /\ want[t] = NoSlot
  /\ allocTo[s] = Nobody
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![t] = s]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<freeList, allocTo, budget>>

CentreVote(c, t) ==
  /\ want[t] # NoSlot
  /\ c \notin tally[t]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<freeList, allocTo, want, budget>>

Allocate(t, s) ==
  /\ want[t] = s
  /\ Cardinality(tally[t]) >= Quorum
  /\ s \in freeList
  /\ freeList' = freeList \ {s}
  /\ allocTo' = [allocTo EXCEPT ![s] = t]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![t] = NoSlot]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED budget

\* The override skips the vote, never the bookkeeping.
ForceAllocate(t, s) ==
  /\ budget > 0
  /\ want[t] = s
  /\ s \in freeList
  /\ freeList' = freeList \ {s}
  /\ allocTo' = [allocTo EXCEPT ![s] = t]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![t] = NoSlot]
  /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ budget' = budget - 1

ReleaseSlot(t, s) ==
  /\ allocTo[s] = t
  /\ allocTo' = [allocTo EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ freeList' = freeList \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<want, tally, budget>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Centres, t \in Trains : CentreVote(c, t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, s \in Slots :
        AskFor(t, s) \/ Allocate(t, s) \/ ForceAllocate(t, s) \/ ReleaseSlot(t, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

nl:
A subway signalling system allocates junction path slots to trains. A slot may belong to one
train at a time; handing the same slot to two trains routes them through the junction
together. The signalling centres keep two books for this: a free list of the slots currently
available, and an allocation table saying which train holds each slot. The two books are
supposed to be exact complements of one another, and a slot that is handed out while still
sitting on the free list is precisely how the same slot ends up allocated twice.

A train driver asks for a specific slot. The signalling centres then vote on the request, and
the allocation goes through once a quorum of distinct centres has voted for it: the slot
comes off the free list and the allocation table records the train. The duty controller holds
a privileged override and can push a pending request straight through without any votes, out
of a limited daily budget; the override skips the vote, not the books -- it still takes the
slot off the free list as it writes the allocation. When a train has cleared the junction it
releases its slot, which clears the table entry and puts the slot back on the free list.

The actions are: a train asks for a slot that is currently unallocated, a signalling centre
votes for a pending request, allocate a slot to a request that has reached quorum, the duty
controller spends one override to allocate a pending request without votes, and a train
releases a slot it holds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is on the free list exactly when the allocation table shows it as
held by nobody, so no allocated slot can ever be handed out a second time from the free list.
